item.title: SCP-5925:
item.content:encoded: I'm so very glad this made it to the main list. It's a fun concept and escalates tension excellently within the small space it has. That brief moment between the cold settling in and the doctor acting under pressure adds so much. It's a clever piece.

item.title: SCP-5298:
item.content:encoded: Props for implying the purpose of the new object class. I'm frustrated that the dialogue isn't funny — extradimensional boogeymen saying "Jesus fuck!" and interdimensional agents saying "Thank JALAKARA!" aren't jokes — and that only deflates the physical comedy and general humor of robot children for a boogeyman sting op. I think this would work a lot better if the whole article was separated from the Three Moons Initiative entirely and was instead tied to the faerie folk; fairy tale crime is a fun genre of urban fantasy that opens itself up to less awkward referential comedy.

item.title: SCP-5871: Re: Just Something To Keep In Mind
item.content:encoded: If it's going to be short, it has to do something special, fast. It has to provide some sort of twist, swerve, revelation that makes the reader think "wow, you got there with the minimum words required, that's incredible." It can't just be a short description with crosslinks to other people's stuff.

item.title: SCP-5668: Re: ?
item.content:encoded:
I'm not supposed to reply or comment after a deletion vote is called but this is important.

1, you're supposed to get critique before posting.

2, there's just very little here. The dialogue is clunky and the story you have is very short and boring. You should choose a specific thing to write a narrative around. Who is that doctor? What does Manitoba have to do with the SCP? How do they communicate? These are all possible narratives you could focus on.

3. There's numerous formatting errors.
